Paragraph.Text: the estimated amount of the proceeds of disposition to be received by the non-resident person for the property; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of the adjusted cost base to the non-resident person of the property at the time of the sending of the notice.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Certificate in respect of proposed disposition
Subsection.Text: Where a non-resident person who has sent to the Minister a notice under subsection 116(1) in respect of a proposed disposition of any property has

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: paid to the Receiver General, as or on account of tax under this Part payable by the non-resident person for the year, 25% of the amount, if any, by which the estimated amount set out in the notice in accordance with paragraph 116(1)(c) exceeds the amount set out in the notice in accordance with paragraph 116(1)(d), or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: furnished the Minister with security acceptable to the Minister in respect of the proposed disposition of the property,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: the Minister shall forthwith issue to the non-resident person and the proposed purchaser a certificate in prescribed form in respect of the proposed disposition, fixing therein an amount (in this section referred to as the “certificate limit”) equal to the estimated amount set out in the notice in accordance with paragraph 116(1)(c).

Subsection.Text: Every non-resident person who in a taxation year disposes of any taxable Canadian property of that person (other than property described in subsection 116(5.2) and excluded property) shall, not later than 10 days after the disposition, send to the Minister, by registered mail, a notice setting out

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the name and address of the person to whom the non-resident person disposed of the property (in this section referred to as the “purchaser”),

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a description of the property sufficient to identify it, and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a statement of the proceeds of disposition of the property and the amount of its adjusted cost base to the non-resident person immediately before the disposition,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: unless the non-resident person has, at any time before the disposition, sent to the Minister a notice under subsection 116(1) in respect of any proposed disposition of that property and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the purchaser was the proposed purchaser referred to in that notice,

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the estimated amount set out in that notice in accordance with paragraph 116(1)(c) is equal to or greater than the proceeds of disposition of the property, and

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: the amount set out in that notice in accordance with paragraph 116(1)(d) does not exceed the adjusted cost base to the non-resident person of the property immediately before the disposition.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Certificate in respect of property disposed of
Subsection.Text: Where a non-resident person who has sent to the Minister a notice under subsection 116(3) in respect of a disposition of any property has

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: paid to the Receiver General, as or on account of tax under this Part payable by the non-resident person for the year, 25% of the amount, if any, by which the proceeds of disposition of the property exceed the adjusted cost base to the non-resident person of the property immediately before the disposition, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: furnished the Minister with security acceptable to the Minister in respect of the disposition of the property,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: the Minister shall forthwith issue to the non-resident person and the purchaser a certificate in prescribed form in respect of the disposition.

Subsection.Text: Where in a taxation year a purchaser has acquired from a non-resident person any taxable Canadian property (other than depreciable property or excluded property) of the non-resident person, the purchaser, unless

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: after reasonable inquiry the purchaser had no reason to believe that the non-resident person was not resident in Canada,

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: subsection (5.01) applies to the acquisition, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a certificate under subsection 116(4) has been issued to the purchaser by the Minister in respect of the property,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: is liable to pay, and shall remit to the Receiver General within 30 days after the end of the month in which the purchaser acquired the property, as tax under this Part for the year on behalf of the non-resident person, 25% of the amount, if any, by which

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the cost to the purchaser of the property so acquired

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: exceeds

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the certificate limit fixed by the certificate, if any, issued under subsection 116(2) in respect of the disposition of the property by the non-resident person to the purchaser,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: and is entitled to deduct or withhold from any amount paid or credited by the purchaser to the non-resident person or otherwise recover from the non-resident person any amount paid by the purchaser as such a tax.

Subsection.Text: This subsection applies to the acquisition of a property by a person (referred to in this subsection as the “purchaser”) from a non-resident person if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the purchaser concludes after reasonable inquiry that the non-resident person is, under a tax treaty that Canada has with a particular country, resident in the particular country;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the property would be treaty-protected property of the non-resident person if the non-resident person were, under the tax treaty referred to in paragraph (a), resident in the particular country; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the purchaser provides notice under subsection (5.02) in respect of the acquisition.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Notice by purchaser in respect of an acquisition of property
Subsection.Text: A person (referred to in this subsection as the “purchaser”) who acquires property from a non-resident person provides notice under this subsection in respect of the acquisition if the purchaser sends to the Minister, on or before the day that is 30 days after the date of the acquisition, a notice setting out

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the date of the acquisition;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the name and address of the non-resident person;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a description of the property sufficient to identify it;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the amount paid or payable, as the case may be, by the purchaser for the property; and

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the name of the country with which Canada has concluded a tax treaty under which the property is a treaty-protected property for the purposes of subsection (5.01) or (6.1), as the case may be.

Subsection.Text: If a non-resident person has disposed of or proposes to dispose of a life insurance policy in Canada, a Canadian resource property or a taxable Canadian property other than

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: excluded property, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: property that has been transferred or distributed on or after the non-resident person’s death and as a consequence thereof

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: to any person by way of gift inter vivos or to a person with whom the non-resident person was not dealing at arm’s length for no proceeds of disposition or for proceeds of disposition less than the fair market value of the property at the time the non-resident person so disposed of it or proposes to dispose of it, as the case may be, the following rules apply:

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the reference in paragraph 116(1)(c) to “the proceeds of disposition to be received by the non-resident person for the property” shall be read as a reference to “the fair market value of the property at the time the non-resident person proposes to dispose of it”,

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the references in subsections 116(3) and (4) to “the proceeds of disposition of the property” shall be read as references to “the fair market value of the property immediately before the disposition”,

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: the references in subsection 116(5) to “the cost to the purchaser of the property so acquired” shall be read as references to “the fair market value of the property at the time it was so acquired”, and

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: the reference in subsection 116(5.3) to “the amount payable by the taxpayer for the property so acquired” shall be read as a reference to “the fair market value of the property at the time it was so acquired”.

Subsection.Text: If a non-resident person has, in respect of a disposition, or a proposed disposition, in a taxation year to a taxpayer of property (other than excluded property) that is a life insurance policy in Canada, a Canadian resource property, a property (other than capital property) that is real property, or an immovable, situated in Canada, a timber resource property, depreciable property that is a taxable Canadian property or any interest in, or for civil law any right in, or any option in respect of, a property to which this subsection applies (whether or not that property exists),

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: paid to the Receiver General, as or on account of tax under this Part payable by the non-resident person for the year, such amount as is acceptable to the Minister in respect of the disposition or proposed disposition of the property, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: furnished the Minister with security acceptable to the Minister in respect of the disposition or proposed disposition of the property,

ContinuedSectionSubsection.Text: the Minister shall forthwith issue to the non-resident person and to the taxpayer a certificate in prescribed form in respect of the disposition or proposed disposition fixing therein an amount equal to the proceeds of disposition, proposed proceeds of disposition or such other amount as is reasonable in the circumstances.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Liability of purchaser in certain cases
Subsection.Text: Where in a taxation year a taxpayer has acquired from a non-resident person property referred to in subsection 116(5.2),

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the taxpayer, unless subsection (5.01) applies to the acquisition or unless after reasonable inquiry the taxpayer had no reason to believe that the non-resident person was not resident in Canada, is liable to pay, as tax under this Part for the year on behalf of the non-resident person, 50% of the amount, if any, by which

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount payable by the taxpayer for the property so acquired

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount fixed in the certificate, if any, issued under subsection 116(5.2) in respect of the disposition of the property by the non-resident person to the taxpayer

ContinuedParagraph.Text: and is entitled to deduct or withhold from any amount paid or credited by the taxpayer to the non-resident person or to otherwise recover from the non-resident person any amount paid by the taxpayer as such a tax; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the taxpayer shall, within 30 days after the end of the month in which the taxpayer acquired the property, remit to the Receiver General the tax for which the taxpayer is liable under paragraph 116(5.3)(a).

Subsection.Text: Where there has been a disposition by a non-resident of a life insurance policy in Canada by virtue of subsection 148(2) or any of paragraphs (a) to (c) and (e) of the definition disposition in subsection 148(9), the insurer under the policy shall, for the purposes of subsections 116(5.2) and (5.3) be deemed to be the taxpayer who acquired the property for an amount equal to the proceeds of disposition as determined under section 148.
For the purposes of this section, excluded property of a non-resident person means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a property that is a taxable Canadian property solely because a provision of this Act deems it to be a taxable Canadian property;

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: a property (other than real or immovable property situated in Canada, a Canadian resource property or a timber resource property) that is described in an inventory of a business carried on in Canada by the person;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a security that is

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: listed on a recognized stock exchange, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: either

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: a share of the capital stock of a corporation, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: SIFT wind-up entity equity;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a unit of a mutual fund trust;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: a bond, debenture, bill, note, mortgage, hypothecary claim or similar obligation;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: property of a non-resident insurer that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is licensed or otherwise authorized under the laws of Canada or a province to carry on an insurance business in Canada, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: carries on an insurance business, within the meaning of subsection 138(1) of the Act, in Canada;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: property of an authorized foreign bank that carries on a Canadian banking business;

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: an option in respect of property referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (f) whether or not such property is in existence;

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: an interest, or for civil law a right, in property referred to in any of paragraphs (a) to (g); and

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: a property that is, at the time of its disposition, a treaty-exempt property of the person.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of subsection (6), a property is a treaty-exempt property of a non-resident person, at the time of the non-resident person’s disposition of the property to another person (referred to in this subsection as the “purchaser”), if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: it is, at that time, a treaty-protected property of the non-resident person; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: where the purchaser and the non-resident person are related at that time, the purchaser provides notice under subsection (5.02) in respect of the disposition.

Subsection.Text: The definitions in subsection 138(12) apply to this section.

If, in the absence of this subsection, the Minister would be required to issue a certificate under subsection (2), (4) or (5.2) in respect of a disposition, or a proposed disposition, of property that is residential property, as defined in section 2 of the Underused Housing Tax Act, the Minister may decline to issue the certificate if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the Minister is not satisfied that all returns that the non-resident person is required to file under section 7 of that Act in respect of the property have been filed;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the Minister is not satisfied that all taxes and other amounts payable under that Act by the non-resident person have been paid; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the following conditions are met:

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that, for the calendar year immediately preceding the calendar year in which the property is or is expected to be disposed of, the non-resident person will be required to file a return under section 7 of that Act in respect of the property or will become liable to pay an amount of tax under subsection 6(3) of that Act in respect of the property, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the return has not been filed or the amount of tax has not been paid.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this Division, except section 120 (other than subparagraph (a)(ii) of the definition tax otherwise payable under this Part in subsection 120(4)), tax payable under this Part, tax otherwise payable under this Part and tax under this Part shall be computed as if this Part were read without reference to Division E.1.

The tax payable under this Part by an individual on the individual’s taxable income or taxable income earned in Canada, as the case may be (in this Subdivision referred to as the “amount taxable”) for a taxation year is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: 14% of the amount taxable, if the amount taxable is equal to or less than the amount determined for the taxation year in respect of $57,375;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the amount taxable is greater than $57,375, but is equal to or less than $114,750, the maximum amount determinable in respect of the taxation year under paragraph (a), plus 20.5% of the amount by which the amount taxable exceeds $57,375 for the year;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the amount taxable is greater than $114,750, but is equal to or less than $177,882, the maximum amount determinable in respect of the taxation year under paragraph (b), plus 26% of the amount by which the amount taxable exceeds $114,750 for the year;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: if the amount taxable is greater than $177,882, but is equal to or less than $253,414, the maximum amount determinable in respect of the taxation year under paragraph (c), plus 29% of the amount by which the amount taxable exceeds $177,882 for the year; and

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: if the amount taxable is greater than $253,414, the maximum amount determinable in respect of the taxation year under paragraph (d), plus 33% of the amount by which the amount taxable exceeds $253,414 for the year.

Subsection.MarginalNote: Adjustment to tax payable – advance payment
Subsection.Text: The tax payable under this Part on the individual’s taxable income for a taxation year, as computed under subsection (2), is deemed to be the total of the amount otherwise computed under that subsection and, except for the purposes of sections 118 to 118.9, 120.2, 121 and Subdivision C, the lesser of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the total of all amounts deemed to have been paid on account of the individual’s tax payable under this Part for the taxation year under subsections 122.7(2) and (3), and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the amount that

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: if the individual is an eligible individual for the purposes of subsection 122.7(2), is the total of all amounts deemed to have been paid

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: on account of the individual’s tax payable under this Part for the taxation year under subsection 122.72(1) or (3), and

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: on account of tax payable under this Part for the taxation year under subsection 122.72(1) or (3), if subsection 122.72(1) were read without reference to subsection 122.7(3), of a person who is the individual’s cohabiting spouse or common-law partner (as defined in subsection 122.7(1)) at the end of the taxation year, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: in any other case, is the total of all amounts deemed to have been paid on account of the individual’s tax payable under this Part for the taxation year under subsection 122.72(1) or (3), if subsection 122.72(1) were read without reference to subsection 122.7(2).

Subsection.Text: Each of the amounts of $30,754, $61,509 and $100,000 referred to in subsection (2) is deemed, for the purposes of applying subsection (2) to the 2004 taxation year, to be the greater of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount that would be used for the 2004 taxation year if this section were read without reference to this subsection, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount of $30,754, $35,000,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount of $61,509, $70,000, and

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Heading.TitleText: Annual Adjustment of Deductions and Other Amounts

Subsection.Text: Each specified amount in relation to tax payable under this Part or Part I.2 for a taxation year shall be adjusted so that the amount to be used for the year under the provision for which the amount is relevant is the total of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount that would, but for subsection (3), be the amount to be used under the relevant provision for the preceding taxation year, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the product obtained by multiplying

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount referred to in paragraph (a)

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount, adjusted in such manner as may be prescribed and rounded to the nearest one-thousandth, or, where the result obtained is equidistant from two consecutive one-thousandths, to the higher thereof, that is determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period that ended on September 30 next before that year, and
is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period immediately preceding the period mentioned in the description of A.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subsection (1), each of the following amounts is a specified amount in relation to tax payable under this Part or Part I.2 for a taxation year:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $300 referred to in subparagraph 6(1)(b)(v.1);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $1,000 referred to in the formula in paragraph 8(1)(s);

Paragraph.Label: (b.1)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $10,000 referred to in subparagraph 8(1)(t)(i), for a taxation year that begins after 2026;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $625,000 referred to in paragraph 110.6(2)(a), for a taxation year that begins after 2025;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in subsection 117(2);

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in the description of B in subsection 118(1);

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $12,298 in the description of A in subsection 118(1.1);

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $15,000 in paragraph (d) of the description of F in subsection 118(1.1);

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in subsection 118(2);

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $1,000 referred to in subsection 118(10);

Paragraph.Label: (j)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $15,000 referred to in subsection 118.01(2);

Paragraph.Label: (k)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in subsection 118.2(1);

Paragraph.Label: (l)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in subsection 118.3(1);

Paragraph.Label: (m)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in subsection 122.5(3);

Paragraph.Label: (m.1)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in subsection 122.5(3.005), for a taxation year that begins after 2026;

Paragraph.Label: (n)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $2,500 referred to in subsection 122.51(1);

Paragraph.Label: (o)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in subsection 122.51(2);

Paragraph.Label: (p)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $14,000 referred to in subsection 122.7(1.3);

Paragraph.Label: (q)
Paragraph.Text: the amounts of $1,395 and $2,403 in the description of A, and each of the amounts expressed in dollars in the description of B, in subsection 122.7(2);

Paragraph.Label: (r)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $720 in the description of C, and each of the amounts expressed in dollars in the description of D, in subsection 122.7(3);

Paragraph.Label: (s)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of $10,000 in the description of B in subsection 122.91(2); and

Paragraph.Label: (t)
Paragraph.Text: each of the amounts expressed in dollars in Part I.2.

Subsection.Text: Where an amount referred to in this section, when adjusted as provided in this section, is not a multiple of one dollar, it shall be rounded to the nearest multiple of one dollar or, where it is equidistant from two such consecutive multiples, to the higher thereof.
In this section, the Consumer Price Index for any 12 month period is the result arrived at by

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: aggregating the Consumer Price Index for Canada, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act, adjusted in such manner as is prescribed, for each month in that period;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: dividing the aggregate obtained under paragraph 117.1(4)(a) by twelve; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: rounding the result obtained under paragraph 117.1(4)(b) to the nearest one-thousandth or, where the result obtained is equidistant from two consecutive one-thousandths, to the higher thereof.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of computing the tax payable under this Part by an individual for a taxation year, there may be deducted an amount determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the appropriate percentage for the year, and
is the total of,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of an individual who at any time in the year is a married person or a person who is in a common-law partnership who supports the individual’s spouse or common-law partner and is not living separate and apart from the spouse or common-law partner by reason of a breakdown of their marriage or common-law partnership, an amount equal to the total of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the basic personal amount of the individual for the year, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is

FormulaParagraph.Label: (A)
FormulaParagraph.Text: $2,150 if the spouse or common-law partner is dependent on the individual by reason of mental or physical infirmity, and

FormulaParagraph.Label: (B)
FormulaParagraph.Text: in any other case, nil,

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the basic personal amount of the individual for the year, and

is the income of the individual’s spouse or common-law partner for the year or, if the individual and the individual’s spouse or common-law partner are living separate and apart at the end of the year because of a breakdown of their marriage or common-law partnership, the spouse’s or common-law partner’s income for the year while married to, or in a common-law partnership with, the individual and not so separated,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of an individual who does not claim a deduction for the year because of paragraph 118(1)(a) and who, at any time in the year,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: is

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: a person who is unmarried and who does not live in a common-law partnership, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: a person who is married or in a common-law partnership, who neither supported nor lived with their spouse or common-law partner and who is not supported by that spouse or common-law partner, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: whether alone or jointly with one or more other persons, maintains a self-contained domestic establishment (in which the individual lives) and actually supports in that establishment a person who, at that time, is

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: except in the case of a child of the individual, resident in Canada,

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: wholly dependent for support on the individual, or the individual and the other person or persons, as the case may be,

Clause.Label: (C)
Clause.Text: related to the individual, and

Clause.Label: (D)
Clause.Text: except in the case of a parent or grandparent of the individual, either under 18 years of age or so dependent by reason of mental or physical infirmity,

ContinuedParagraph.Text: an amount equal to the total of

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: the basic personal amount of the individual for the year, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is

FormulaParagraph.Label: (I)
FormulaParagraph.Text: the dependent person is, at the end of the taxation year, 18 years of age or older and is, at any time in the year, dependent on the individual by reason of mental or physical infirmity, or

FormulaParagraph.Label: (II)
FormulaParagraph.Text: the dependent person is a person, other than a child of the individual in respect of whom paragraph (b.1) applies, who, at the end of the taxation year, is under the age of 18 years and who, by reason of mental or physical infirmity, is likely to be, for a long and continuous period of indefinite duration, dependent on others for significantly more assistance in attending to the dependent person’s personal needs and care, when compared to persons of the same age, and is so dependent on the individual at any time in the year, and

FormulaParagraph.Label: (B)
FormulaParagraph.Text: in any other case, nil,

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the basic personal amount of the individual for the year, and
is the dependent person’s income for the year,

Paragraph.Label: (b.1)
Paragraph.Text: $2,150 for each child, who is under the age of 18 years at the end of the taxation year, of the individual and who, by reason of mental or physical infirmity, is likely to be, for a long and continuous period of indefinite duration, dependent on others for significantly more assistance in attending to the child’s personal needs and care, when compared to children of the same age if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the child ordinarily resides throughout the taxation year with the individual together with another parent of the child, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: except if subparagraph (i) applies, the individual

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: may deduct an amount under paragraph (b) in respect of the child, or

Clause.Label: (B)

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subsection 118(1), the following rules apply:

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: no amount may be deducted under subsection 118(1) because of paragraphs (a) and (b) of the description of B in subsection 118(1) by an individual in a taxation year for more than one other person;

Paragraph.Label: (a.1)
Paragraph.Text: no amount may be deducted under subsection (1) because of paragraph (b) of the description of B in subsection (1) by an individual for a taxation year for a person in respect of whom an amount is deducted because of paragraph (a) of that description by another individual for the year if, throughout the year, the person and that other individual are married to each other or in a common-law partnership with each other and are not living separate and apart because of a breakdown of their marriage or the common-law partnership, as the case may be;

Paragraph.Label: (a.2)
Paragraph.Text: a reference to income for a year is to be read as a reference to that income determined as if, in computing that income, no amount were deductible under paragraph 20(1)(ww);

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: not more than one individual is entitled to a deduction under subsection (1) because of paragraph (b) of the description of B in that subsection for a taxation year in respect of the same person or the same domestic establishment and where two or more individuals otherwise entitled to such a deduction fail to agree as to the individual by whom the deduction may be made, no such deduction for the year shall be allowed to either or any of them;

Paragraph.Label: (b.1)
Paragraph.Text: not more than one individual is entitled to a deduction under subsection (1) because of paragraph (b.1) of the description of B in that subsection for a taxation year in respect of the same child and where two or more individuals otherwise entitled to such a deduction fail to agree as to the individual by whom the deduction may be made, no such deduction for the year shall be allowed to either or any of them;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if an individual is entitled to a deduction under subsection (1) because of paragraph (a) or (b) of the description of B in subsection (1) for a taxation year in respect of any person, no amount may be deducted because of paragraph (d) of that description by any individual for the year in respect of the person; and

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: if more than one individual is entitled to a deduction under subsection (1) because of paragraph (d) of the description of B in subsection (1) for a taxation year in respect of the same person,

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the total of all amounts so deductible for the year shall not exceed the maximum amount that would be so deductible for the year by any one of those individuals for that person if that individual were the only individual entitled to deduct an amount for the year because of that paragraph for that person, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: if the individuals cannot agree as to what portion of the amount each can so deduct, the Minister may fix the portions.

Subsection.Text: No amount may be deducted under subsection (1) in computing an individual’s tax payable under this Part for a taxation year in respect of a person where the individual is required to pay a support amount (within the meaning assigned by subsection 56.1(4)) to the individual’s spouse or common-law partner or former spouse or common-law partner in respect of the person and the individual

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: lives separate and apart from the spouse or common-law partner or former spouse or common-law partner throughout the year because of the breakdown of their marriage or common-law partnership; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: claims a deduction for the year because of section 60 in respect of a support amount paid to the spouse or common-law partner or former spouse or common-law partner.

Subsection.Text: Where, if this Act were read without reference to this subsection, solely because of the application of subsection (5), no individual is entitled to a deduction under paragraph (b) or (b.1) of the description of B in subsection (1) for a taxation year in respect of a child, subsection (5) shall not apply in respect of that child for that taxation year.

For the purposes of paragraph (d) of the description of B in subsection (1), dependant, of an individual for a taxation year, means a person who at any time in the year is dependent on the individual for support and is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the child or grandchild of the individual or of the individual’s spouse or common-law partner; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the parent, grandparent, brother, sister, uncle, aunt, niece or nephew, if resident in Canada at any time in the year, of the individual or of the individual’s spouse or common-law partner.

Subsection.Text: Subject to subsections (8) and (8.1), for the purposes of this subsection and subsection (3),

Definition.Text: eligible pension income of an individual for a taxation year means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if the individual has attained the age of 65 years before the end of the taxation year, the pension income received by the individ-ual in the taxation year, and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if the individual has not attained the age of 65 years before the end of the taxation year, the qualified pension income received by the individual in the taxation year; (revenu de pension déterminé)

Definition.Text: pension income received by an individual in a taxation year means the total of

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the total of all amounts each of which is an amount included in computing the individual’s income for the year that is

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: a payment in respect of a life annuity out of or under a superannuation or pension plan (other than a pooled registered pension plan) or a specified pension plan,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: an annuity payment under a registered retirement savings plan, under an “amended plan” as referred to in subsection 146(12) or under an annuity in respect of which an amount is included in computing the individual’s income by reason of paragraph 56(1)(d.2),

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: a payment out of or under a registered retirement income fund or under an “amended fund” as referred to in subsection 146.3(11),

Subparagraph.Label: (iii.1)
Subparagraph.Text: a payment (other than a payment described in subparagraph (i)) under a money purchase provision (as defined in subsection 147.1(1)) of a registered pension plan or under a specified pension plan,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii.2)
Subparagraph.Text: an amount included under section 147.5,

Subparagraph.Label: (iii.3)
Subparagraph.Text: an amount included under subsection 146.5(2),

Subparagraph.Label: (iv)
Subparagraph.Text: an annuity payment under a deferred profit sharing plan or under a “revoked plan” as referred to in subsection 147(15),

Subparagraph.Label: (v)
Subparagraph.Text: a payment described in subparagraph 147(2)(k)(v), or

Subparagraph.Label: (vi)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount by which an annuity payment included in computing the individual’s income for the year by reason of paragraph 56(1)(d) exceeds the capital element of that payment as determined or established under paragraph 60(a), and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the total of all amounts each of which is an amount included in computing the individual’s income for the year by reason of section 12.2 of this Act or paragraph 56(1)(d.1) of the Income Tax Act, chapter 148 of the Revised Statutes of Canada, 1952; (revenu de pension)

Definition.Text: qualified pension income received by an individual in a taxation year means the total of all amounts each of which is an amount included in computing the individual’s income for the year and described in

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: subparagraph (a)(i) of the definition pension income in this subsection, or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: any of subparagraphs 118(7) qualified pension income (a)(ii) to 118(7) qualified pension income (a)(vi) or paragraph (b) of the definition pension income in this subsection received by the individual as a consequence of the death of a spouse or common-law partner of the individual. (revenu de pension admissible)

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subsection (7), pension income and qualified pension income received by an individual in a taxation year do not include any amount that is

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of a pension or supplement under the Old Age Security Act or of any similar payment under a law of a province;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the amount of a benefit under the Canada Pension Plan or under a provincial pension plan as defined in section 3 of that Act;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: a death benefit;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: the amount, if any, by which

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: an amount required to be included in computing the individual’s income for the year

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the amount, if any, by which the amount referred to in subparagraph (i) exceeds the total of all amounts deducted (other than under paragraph 60(c)) by the individual for the year in respect of that amount;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: a payment received out of or under a salary deferral arrangement, a retirement compensation arrangement, an employee benefit plan or an employee trust; or

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: a payment (other than a payment under the Judges Act or the Lieutenant Governors Superannuation Act) received out of or under an unfunded supplemental plan or arrangement, being a plan or arrangement where

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the payment was in respect of services rendered to an employer by the individual or the individual’s spouse or common-law partner or former spouse or common-law partner as an employee, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the plan or arrangement would have been a retirement compensation arrangement or an employee benefit plan had the employer made a contribution in respect of the payment to a trust governed by the plan or arrangement.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of subsection (7), a payment in respect of a life annuity under a superannuation or pension plan is deemed to include a payment in respect of bridging benefits, being benefits payable under a registered pension plan on a periodic basis and not less frequently than annually to an individual where

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the individual or the individual’s spouse or common-law partner or former spouse or common-law partner was a member (as defined in subsection 147.1(1)) of the registered pension plan;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the benefits are payable for a period ending no later than the end of the month following the month in which the member attains 65 years of age or would have attained that age if the member had survived to that day; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: the amount (expressed on an annualized basis) of the benefits payable to the individual for a calendar year does not exceed the total of the maximum amount of benefits payable for that year under Part I of the Old Age Security Act and the maximum amount of benefits (other than disability, death or survivor benefits) payable for that year under either the Canada Pension Plan or a provincial pension plan as defined in section 3 of that Act.

Subsection.Text: For greater certainty, in the case of a child who in a taxation year is born, adopted or dies, the reference to “throughout the taxation year” in subparagraph 118(1)(b.1)(i) is to be read as a reference to “throughout the portion of the taxation year that is after the child’s birth or adoption or before the child’s death”.

Subsection.Text: The following definitions apply in this section.

Definition.Text: adoption period, in respect of an eligible child of an individual, means the period that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: begins at the earlier of the time that an application is made for registration with a provincial ministry responsible for adoption (or with an adoption agency licensed by a provincial government) and the time, if any, that an application related to the adoption is made to a Canadian court; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: ends at the later of the time an adoption order is issued by, or recognized by, a government in Canada in respect of that child, and the time that the child first begins to reside permanently with the individual. (période d’adoption)

Definition.Text: eligible adoption expense, in respect of an eligible child of an individual, means an amount paid for expenses incurred during the adoption period in respect of the adoption of that child, including

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: fees paid to an adoption agency licensed by a provincial government;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: court costs and legal and administrative expenses related to an adoption order in respect of that child;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: reasonable and necessary travel and living expenses of that child and the adoptive parents;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: document translation fees;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: mandatory fees paid to a foreign institution;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: mandatory expenses paid in respect of the immigration of that child; and

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: any other reasonable expenses related to the adoption required by a provincial government or an adoption agency licensed by a provincial government. (dépense d’adoption admissible)

Definition.Text: eligible child, of an individual, means a child who has not attained the age of 18 years at the time that an adoption order is issued or recognized by a government in Canada in respect of the adoption of that child by that individual. (enfant admissible)

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of computing the tax payable under this Part by an individual for the taxation year that includes the end of the adoption period in respect of an eligible child of the individual, there may be deducted the amount determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the appropriate percentage for the taxation year; and
is the lesser of

FormulaParagraph.Label: (b)
FormulaParagraph.Text: the amount determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the total of all eligible adoption expenses in respect of the eligible child, and

is the total of all amounts each of which is the amount of a reimbursement or any other form of assistance (other than an amount that is included in computing the individual’s income and that is not deductible in computing the individual’s taxable income) that any individual is or was entitled to receive in respect of an amount included in computing the value of C.

Subsection.Text: Where more than one individual is entitled to a deduction under this section for a taxation year in respect of the adoption of an eligible child, the total of all amounts so deductible shall not exceed the maximum amount that would be so deductible for the year by any one of those individuals for that child if that individual were the only individual entitled to deduct an amount for the year under this section, and if the individuals cannot agree as to what portion of the amount each can so deduct, the Minister may fix the portions.

Subsection.Text: The following definitions apply in this section.

Definition.Text: digital news subscription, of an individual with a qualified Canadian journalism organization, means an agreement entered into between the individual and the qualified Canadian journalism organization, if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the agreement entitles an individual to access content of the qualified Canadian journalism organization in digital form and that content is primarily written news; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the qualified Canadian journalism organization does not hold a licence as defined in subsection 2(1) of the Broadcasting Act. (abonnement aux nouvelles numériques)

Definition.Text: qualifying subscription expense, for a taxation year, means the amount paid in the year for a digital news subscription of an individual with a qualified Canadian journalism organization and, for this purpose, if the digital news subscription provides access to content in non-digital form or content other than content of qualified Canadian journalism organizations, the amount considered to be paid for the digital news subscription shall not exceed

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the cost of a comparable digital news subscription with the qualified Canadian journalism organization that solely provides access to content of qualified Canadian journalism organizations in digital form; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if there is no such comparable digital news subscription, 1/2 of the amount actually paid. (dépense pour abonnement admissible)

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of computing the tax payable under this Part by an individual for a taxation year that is before 2025, there may be deducted the amount determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the appropriate percentage for the year; and
is the lesser of

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the total of all amounts each of which is a qualifying subscription expense of the individual for the year.

Subsection.Text: If more than one individual is entitled to a deduction under this section for a taxation year in respect of a qualifying subscription expense, the total of all amounts so deductible shall not exceed the maximum amount that would be so deductible for the year by any one of those individuals in respect of the qualifying subscription expense, if that individual were the only individual entitled to deduct an amount for the year under this section, and if the individuals cannot agree as to what portion of the amount each can so deduct, the Minister may fix the portions.

For the purposes of subsection (1), if amounts paid under an agreement cease to be qualifying subscription expenses at any particular time in a calendar year and, at the particular time, the Minister has communicated or otherwise made available pursuant to paragraph 241(3.4)(b) that these amounts qualify as qualifying subscription expenses, amounts paid under that agreement are deemed to be qualifying subscription expenses — to the same extent that the amounts paid were considered to be qualifying subscription expenses immediately before the particular time — until the end of the calendar year in which the Minister communicates or otherwise makes available pursuant to paragraph 241(3.4)(b) that amounts paid under the agreement no longer qualify as qualifying subscription expenses.

If an organization enters into a digital news subscription agreement with an individual and amounts paid under the agreement cease to be qualifying subscription expenses, the organization shall inform the individual that amounts paid under the agreement are no longer qualifying subscription expenses.

Subsection.Text: The following definitions apply in this section.

Definition.Text: eligible dwelling of an individual, at any time, means a housing unit (including the land subjacent to the housing unit and the immediately contiguous land, but not including the portion of such land that exceeds the greater of 1/2 hectare and the portion of such land that the individual establishes is necessary for the use and enjoyment of the housing unit as a residence) located in Canada if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the individual (or a trust under which the individual is a beneficiary) owns, whether jointly with another person or otherwise, at that time, the housing unit or a share of the capital stock of a co-operative housing corporation acquired for the sole purpose of acquiring the right to inhabit the housing unit owned by the corporation; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the housing unit is ordinarily inhabited at any time during the eligible period by the individual, by the individual’s spouse or common-law partner or former spouse or common-law partner or by a child of the individual. (logement admissible)

Definition.Text: eligible period means the period that begins on January 28, 2009 and that ends on January 31, 2010. (période d’admissibilité)
individual does not include a trust. (particulier)

qualifying expenditure of an individual means an outlay or expense that is made or incurred, by the individual or by a qualifying relation in respect of the individual during the eligible period, that is directly attributable to a qualifying renovation by the individual and that is the cost of goods acquired or services received during the eligible period and includes such an outlay or expense for permits required for, or for the rental of equipment used in the course of, the qualifying renovation, but does not include such an outlay or expense

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: to acquire goods that have been used, or acquired for use or lease, by the individual or by a qualifying relation in respect of the individual, for any purpose whatever before they were acquired by the individual or the qualifying relation in respect of the individual;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: made or incurred under the terms of an agreement entered into before the eligible period;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: to acquire a property that can be used independently of the qualifying renovation;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: that is the cost of annual, recurring or routine repair or maintenance;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: to acquire a household appliance;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: to acquire an electronic home-entertainment device;

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: for financing costs in respect of the qualifying renovation;

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: made or incurred for the purpose of gaining or producing income from a business or property; or

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of goods or services provided by a person not dealing at arm’s length with the individual, unless the person is registered for the purposes of Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. (dépense admissible)

Definition.Text: qualifying relation in respect of an individual means a person who is the individual’s spouse or common-law partner, or a child of the individual who has not attained the age of 18 years before the end of 2009 (other than a child who was, at any time during the eligible period, a married person, a person who is in a common-law partnership or a person who has a child). (proche admissible)

qualifying renovation by an individual, at any time, means a renovation or alteration, of a property that is at that time an eligible dwelling of the individual or of a qualifying relation in respect of the individual, that is of an enduring nature and that is integral to the eligible dwelling. (travaux de rénovation admissibles)

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this section,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a qualifying expenditure of an individual includes an outlay or expense made or incurred by a co-operative housing corporation, a condominium corporation (or, for civil law, a syndicate of co-owners) or a similar entity (in this paragraph referred to as the “corporation”), in respect of a property that is owned, administered or managed by that corporation, and that includes an eligible dwelling of the individual, to the extent of the individual’s share of that outlay or expense, if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the outlay or expense would be a qualifying expenditure of the corporation if the corporation were a natural person and the property were an eligible dwelling of that natural person, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the corporation has notified the individual, in writing, of the individual’s share of the outlay or expense; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a qualifying expenditure of an individual includes an outlay or expense made or incurred by a trust, in respect of a property owned by the trust that includes an eligible dwelling of the individual, to the extent of the share of that outlay or expense that is reasonably attributable to the individual, having regard to the amount of the outlays or expenses made or incurred in respect of the eligible dwelling of the individual (including, for this purpose, common areas relevant to more than one eligible dwelling), if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the outlay or expense would be a qualifying expenditure of the trust if the trust were a natural person and the property were an eligible dwelling of that natural person, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the trust has notified the individual, in writing, of the individual’s share of the outlay or expense.

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of computing the tax payable under this Part by an individual for the individual’s 2009 taxation year, there may be deducted the amount determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the appropriate percentage for the taxation year; and
is the lesser of $10,000 and the total of all amounts, each of which is a qualifying expenditure of the individual.

Subsection.Text: Notwithstanding paragraph 248(28)(b), an amount may be included in determining both an amount under subsection (3) and under section 118.2 if those amounts otherwise qualify to be included for the purposes of those provisions.

If more than one individual is entitled to a deduction under this section for a taxation year in respect of a qualifying expenditure of an individual, the total of all amounts so deductible shall not exceed the maximum amount that would be so deductible for the year by any one of those individuals in respect of the qualifying expenditure, if that individual were the only individual entitled to deduct an amount for the year under this section, and if the individuals cannot agree as to what portion of the amount each can so deduct, the Minister may fix the portions.

Subsection.Text: The following definitions apply in this section.

Definition.Text: eligible dwelling of an individual, at any time in a taxation year, means a housing unit (including the land subjacent to the housing unit and the immediately contiguous land, but not including the portion of that land that exceeds the greater of ½ hectare and the portion of that land that the individual establishes is necessary for the use and enjoyment of the housing unit as a residence) located in Canada if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the individual (or a trust under which the individual is a beneficiary) owns — whether jointly with another person or otherwise — at that time, the housing unit or a share of the capital stock of a cooperative housing corporation acquired for the sole purpose of acquiring the right to inhabit the housing unit owned by the corporation; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the housing unit is ordinarily inhabited, or is reasonably expected to be ordinarily inhabited, at any time in the taxation year

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: by the individual, if the individual is a qualifying individual, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: by the individual and a qualifying individual, if

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the individual is an eligible individual in respect of the qualifying individual, and

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: the qualifying individual does not, throughout the taxation year, own — whether jointly with another person or otherwise — and ordinarily inhabit another housing unit in Canada. (logement admissible)

Definition.Text: eligible individual, in respect of a qualifying individual for a taxation year, means

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: an individual who is the qualifying individual’s spouse or common-law partner in the year;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: except if paragraph (c) applies, an individual who is entitled to deduct an amount under subsection 118.3(2) for the year in respect of the qualifying individual or would be if no amount was claimed for the year by the qualifying individual under subsection 118.3(1) or by the qualifying individual’s spouse or common-law partner under section 118.8; or

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: in the case of a qualifying individual who has attained the age of 65 before the end of the year, an individual who

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: claimed for the year a deduction under subsection 118(1) in respect of the qualifying individual because of

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: paragraph (b) of the description of B in that subsection, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: paragraph (d) of the description of B in that subsection where the qualifying individual is a parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, brother, sister, aunt, uncle, nephew or niece of the individual, or of the individual’s spouse or common-law partner, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: could have claimed for the year a deduction referred to in subparagraph (i) in respect of the qualifying individual if

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: the qualifying individual had no income for the year,

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: in the case of a deduction referred to in clause (i)(A), the individual were not married and not in a common-law partnership, and

Clause.Label: (C)
Clause.Text: in the case of a deduction under subsection 118(1) because of paragraph (d) of the description of B in that subsection in respect of a qualifying individual who is a dependant (within the meaning of subsection 118(6)) of the individual, the qualifying individual was dependent on the individual because of mental or physical infirmity. (particulier admissible)

Definition.Text: individual does not include a trust. (particulier)

qualifying expenditure of an individual means an outlay or expense that is made or incurred, during a taxation year, that is directly attributable to a qualifying renovation — of an eligible dwelling of a qualifying individual or an eligible individual in respect of a qualifying individual — and that is the cost of goods acquired or services received during the year and includes an outlay or expense for permits required for, or for the rental of equipment used in the course of, the qualifying renovation, but does not include an outlay or expense

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: to acquire a property that can be used independently of the qualifying renovation;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: that is the cost of annual, recurring or routine repair or maintenance;

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: to acquire a household appliance;

Paragraph.Label: (d)
Paragraph.Text: to acquire an electronic home-entertainment device;

Paragraph.Label: (e)
Paragraph.Text: that is the cost of housekeeping, security monitoring, gardening, outdoor maintenance or similar services;

Paragraph.Label: (f)
Paragraph.Text: for financing costs in respect of the qualifying renovation;

Paragraph.Label: (g)
Paragraph.Text: made or incurred primarily for the purpose of increasing or maintaining the value of the eligible dwelling;

Paragraph.Label: (h)
Paragraph.Text: made or incurred for the purpose of gaining or producing income from a business or property;

Paragraph.Label: (i)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of goods or services provided by a person not dealing at arm’s length with the qualifying individual or the eligible individual, unless the person is registered for the purposes of Part IX of the Excise Tax Act;

Paragraph.Label: (j)
Paragraph.Text: to the extent that the outlay or expense can reasonably be considered to have been reimbursed, otherwise than as assistance from the federal or a provincial government including a grant, subsidy, forgivable loan or a deduction from tax; or

Paragraph.Label: (k)
Paragraph.Text: that is included in computing a deduction under section 118.2 for any taxpayer for any taxation year. (dépense admissible)

Definition.Text: qualifying individual, in respect of a taxation year, means an individual

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: who has attained the age of 65 years before the end of the taxation year; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in respect of whom an amount is deductible, or would be deductible if this Act were read without reference to paragraph 118.3(1)(c), under section 118.3 in computing a taxpayer’s tax payable under this Part for the taxation year. (particulier déterminé)

Definition.Text: qualifying renovation means a renovation or alteration of an eligible dwelling of a qualifying individual or an eligible individual in respect of a qualifying individual that

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is of an enduring nature and integral to the eligible dwelling; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: is undertaken to

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: enable the qualifying individual to gain access to, or to be mobile or functional within, the eligible dwelling, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: reduce the risk of harm to the qualifying individual within the eligible dwelling or in gaining access to the dwelling. (travaux de rénovation admissibles)

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of this section,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a qualifying expenditure in respect of an eligible dwelling of a particular individual — who is a qualifying individual or an eligible individual in respect of a qualifying individual — includes an outlay or expense made or incurred by a cooperative housing corporation, a condominium corporation (or, for civil law, a syndicate of co-owners) or a similar entity (in this paragraph referred to as the “corporation”), in respect of a property that is owned, administered or managed by that corporation and that includes the eligible dwelling, to the extent of the share of that outlay or expense that is reasonably attributable to the eligible dwelling, if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the outlay or expense would be a qualifying expenditure of the corporation if the corporation were an individual and the property were an eligible dwelling of that individual, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the corporation has notified, in writing, either the particular individual or, if the particular individual is an eligible individual in respect of a qualifying individual, the qualifying individual, of the share of the outlay or expense that is attributable to the eligible dwelling; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: a qualifying expenditure in respect of an eligible dwelling of a particular individual — who is a qualifying individual or an eligible individual in respect of a qualifying individual — includes an outlay or expense made or incurred by a trust, in respect of a property owned by the trust that includes the eligible dwelling, to the extent of the share of that outlay or expense that is reasonably attributable to the eligible dwelling, having regard to the amount of the outlays or expenses made or incurred in respect of the eligible dwelling (including, for this purpose, common areas relevant to more than one eligible dwelling), if

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the outlay or expense would be a qualifying expenditure of the trust if the trust were an individual and the property were an eligible dwelling of that individual, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the trust has notified, in writing, either the particular individual or, if the particular individual is an eligible individual in respect of a qualifying individual, the qualifying individual, of the share of the outlay or expense that is attributable to the eligible dwelling.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of computing the tax payable under this Part by a qualifying individual or an eligible individual, in respect of an eligible dwelling for a taxation year, there may be deducted the amount determined by the formula

FormulaDefinition.Text: is the appropriate percentage for the taxation year; and
is the lesser of

FormulaParagraph.Label: (b)
FormulaParagraph.Text: the total of all amounts, each of which is a qualifying expenditure of the individual in respect of the eligible dwelling for the taxation year.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of this section,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: a maximum of $20,000 of qualifying expenditures for a taxation year in respect of a qualifying individual can be claimed under subsection (3) by the qualifying individual and all eligible individuals in respect of the qualifying individual;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if there is more than one qualifying individual in respect of an eligible dwelling, a maximum of $20,000 of qualifying expenditures for a taxation year in respect of the eligible dwelling can be claimed under subsection (3) by the qualifying individuals and all eligible individuals in respect of the qualifying individuals; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if more than one individual is entitled to a deduction under subsection (3) for a taxation year in respect of the same qualifying individual or the same eligible dwelling and the individuals cannot agree as to what portion of the amount each can so deduct, the Minister may fix the portions.

Subsection.Text: For the purpose of subsection (5), if an individual becomes bankrupt in a particular calendar year, despite subsection 128(2), any reference to the taxation year of the individual is deemed to be a reference to the particular calendar year.

Subsection.MarginalNote: In the event of death and bankruptcy
Subsection.Text: For the purpose of this section,

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: if an individual dies during a calendar year and would have attained 65 years of age if the individual were alive at the end of the year, the individual is deemed to have attained 65 years of age at the beginning of the year;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: if an individual becomes a qualifying individual during a calendar year and becomes bankrupt in that year, the individual is deemed to be a qualifying individual at the beginning of that year; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if an individual becomes a qualifying individual during a calendar year and an eligible individual in respect of the qualifying individual becomes bankrupt in that year, the individual is deemed to be a qualifying individual at the beginning of the year.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: The following definitions apply in this section.

Definition.Text: qualifying home in respect of an individual, means a qualifying home as defined in subsection 146.01(1) that is acquired, whether jointly or otherwise, after January 27, 2009 if

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: the home is acquired by the individual, or by the individual’s spouse or common-law partner, and

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the individual intends to inhabit the home as a principal place of residence not later than one year after its acquisition,

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the individual did not own, whether jointly or otherwise, a home that was occupied by the individual in the period

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: that began at the beginning of the fourth preceding calendar year that ended before the acquisition, and

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: that ended on the day before the acquisition, and

Subparagraph.Label: (iii)
Subparagraph.Text: the individual’s spouse or common-law partner did not, in the period referred to in subparagraph (ii), own, whether jointly or otherwise, a home

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: that was inhabited by the individual during the marriage to or common-law partnership with the individual, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: that was a share of the capital stock of a cooperative housing corporation that relates to a housing unit inhabited by the individual during the marriage to or common-law partnership with the individual; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: the home is acquired by the individual for the benefit of a specified person in respect of the individual, and

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: the individual intends that the home be inhabited by the specified person as a principal place of residence not later than one year after its acquisition by the individual, and

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: the purpose of the acquisition of the home by the individual is to enable the specified person to live in

Clause.Label: (A)
Clause.Text: a home that is more accessible by the specified person or in which the specified person is more mobile or functional, or

Clause.Label: (B)
Clause.Text: an environment better suited to the specified person’s personal needs and care. (habitation admissible)

Definition.Text: specified person in respect of an individual, at any time, means a person who

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: is the individual or is related at that time to the individual; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: would be entitled to a deduction under subsection 118.3(1) in computing tax payable under this Part for the person’s taxation year that includes that time if that subsection were read without reference to paragraph (c) of that subsection. (personne déterminée)

Subsection.Text: For the purposes of this section, an individual is considered to have acquired a qualifying home only if the individual’s interest (or for civil law, right) in it is registered in accordance with the land registration system or other similar system applicable where it is located.

In computing the tax payable under this Part by an individual for a taxation year in which a qualifying home in respect of the individual is acquired, there may be deducted the amount determined by multiplying $10,000 by the appropriate percentage for the taxation year.

If more than one individual is entitled to a deduction under this section for a taxation year in respect of a particular qualifying home, the total of all amounts so deductible shall not exceed the maximum amount that would be so deductible for the year by any one of those individuals in respect of the qualifying home, if that individual were the only individual entitled to deduct an amount for the year under this section, and if the individuals cannot agree as to what portion of the amount each can so deduct, the Minister may fix the portions.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Section.MarginalNote: Definition of eligible volunteer firefighting services

Subsection.Text: In this section and section 118.07, eligible volunteer firefighting services means services provided by an individual in the individual’s capacity as a volunteer firefighter to a fire department that consist primarily of responding to and being on call for firefighting and related emergency calls, attending meetings held by the fire department and participating in required training related to the prevention or suppression of fires, but does not include services provided to a particular fire department if the individual provides firefighting services to the department otherwise than as a volunteer.

For the purpose of computing the tax payable under this Part for a taxation year by an individual who performs eligible volunteer firefighting services in the year, there may be deducted the amount determined by multiplying $6,000 by the appropriate percentage for the taxation year if the individual

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: performs in the year not less than 200 hours of service each of which is an hour of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: eligible volunteer firefighting service for a fire department, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: eligible search and rescue volunteer service for an eligible search and rescue organization; and

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: provides the certificates referred to in subsections (3) and 118.07(3) as and when requested by the Minister.

Subsection.Text: If the Minister so demands, an individual making a claim under this section in respect of a taxation year shall provide to the Minister a written certificate from the fire chief or a delegated official of each fire department to which the individual provided eligible volunteer firefighting services for the year, attesting to the number of hours of eligible volunteer firefighting services performed in the year by the individual for the particular fire department.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: The following definitions apply in this section and section 118.06.

Definition.Text: eligible search and rescue organization means a search and rescue organization

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: that is a member of the Search and Rescue Volunteer Association of Canada, the Civil Air Search and Rescue Association or the Canadian Coast Guard Auxiliary; or

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: whose status as a search and rescue organization is recognized by a provincial, municipal or public authority. (organisme admissible de recherche et sauvetage)

Definition.Text: eligible search and rescue volunteer services means services, other than eligible volunteer firefighting services, provided by an individual in the individual’s capacity as a volunteer to an eligible search and rescue organization that consist primarily of responding to and being on call for search and rescue and related emergency calls, attending meetings held by the organization and participating in required training related to search and rescue services, but does not include services provided to an organization if the individual provides search and rescue services to the organization otherwise than as a volunteer. (services admissibles de volontaire en recherche et sauvetage)

Subsection.MarginalNote: Search and rescue volunteer tax credit
Subsection.Text: For the purpose of computing the tax payable under this Part for a taxation year by an individual who performs eligible search and rescue volunteer services in the year, there may be deducted the amount determined by multiplying $6,000 by the appropriate percentage for the taxation year if the individual

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: performs in the year not less than 200 hours of service each of which is an hour of

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: eligible search and rescue volunteer service for an eligible search and rescue organization, or

Subparagraph.Label: (ii)
Subparagraph.Text: eligible volunteer firefighting services for a fire department;

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: provides the certificates referred to in subsections (3) and 118.06(3) as and when requested by the Minister; and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: has not deducted an amount under section 118.06 for the year.

Subsection.Text: If the Minister so demands, an individual making a claim under this section in respect of a taxation year shall provide to the Minister a written certificate from the team president, or other individual who fulfils a similar role, of each eligible search and rescue organization to which the individual provided eligible search and rescue volunteer services for the year, attesting to the number of hours of eligible search and rescue volunteer services performed in the year by the individual for the particular organization.

HistoricalNote.HistoricalNoteSubItem: [NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated text; see relevant amending Acts and regulations.]

Subsection.Text: In this section,

Definition.Text: total charitable gifts, of an individual for a particular taxation year, means the total of all amounts each of which is the eligible amount — to the extent it is not otherwise included in determining an amount that is deducted under this section in computing any individual’s tax payable under this Part for any taxation year — of a gift (other than a gift any part of the eligible amount of which is included in the total cultural gifts or the total ecological gifts of any individual for any taxation year) that is made

Paragraph.Label: (a)
Paragraph.Text: to a qualified donee,

Paragraph.Label: (b)
Paragraph.Text: in a taxation year that is not a year for which an amount is deducted under subsection 110(2) in computing the individual’s taxable income, and

Paragraph.Label: (c)
Paragraph.Text: if the individual is

Subparagraph.Label: (i)
Subparagraph.Text: not a trust,
